job_description:
About the role
We are looking for a Senior Backend Engineer to join our payments platform team. You will design, build and run the Python services that move money between our customers and their banks, and you will own them in production.

What you will do
- Design and build REST and event-driven services in Python (FastAPI) on top of PostgreSQL.
- Run those services on Kubernetes in AWS, with sensible monitoring and alerting.
- Lead technical design reviews and mentor two mid-level engineers on the team.
- Work with product and compliance to ship features that meet PCI DSS requirements.

What we are looking for
- 6+ years of backend development, at least 3 of them with Python.
- Deep experience with relational databases, ideally PostgreSQL, including query tuning.
- Experience operating services on Kubernetes.
- Clear written communication; we work across three time zones.

Nice to have: Kafka, Terraform, prior fintech experience.
notes: A typical well-structured posting: the summary should keep level, role and the core stack.

job_description:
Mid-level Frontend Developer (React)

Our design-tools startup is growing and we need a frontend developer who cares about the details. You will join a squad of five and work on the editor that thousands of designers use every day.

Responsibilities
- Build new editor features in React and TypeScript.
- Improve rendering performance of large canvases.
- Make the product accessible: keyboard navigation, screen readers, WCAG 2.1 AA.
- Write unit and end-to-end tests (Jest, Playwright).
- Review pull requests and share knowledge in our weekly frontend guild.

Requirements
- 3 to 5 years of professional frontend experience.
- Strong React and TypeScript skills.
- Hands-on experience with web accessibility.
- Comfortable with browser performance tooling.

We offer a hybrid setup (two office days in Lisbon), a learning budget and a calm, kind team.
notes: Mid-level frontend role; accessibility is a core requirement, not a nice-to-have.

job_description:
Junior Data Analyst - Retail Insights

Join the insights team of a national grocery chain. You will turn sales and loyalty-card data into reports and dashboards that store managers actually read. This is an entry-level role with structured training and a dedicated mentor for your first six months.

In this role you will:
* Write SQL queries against our data warehouse (BigQuery) to answer business questions.
* Build and maintain dashboards in Tableau for the regional operations teams.
* Clean and validate data, and document what each metric means.
* Present findings to non-technical stakeholders once a month.

You bring:
* A degree in a quantitative field, or equivalent experience.
* Solid SQL basics; some Python or R is a plus.
* Curiosity and the patience to check numbers twice.

Salary band and benefits are listed on our careers page. Applications close at the end of the month.
notes: Entry-level analyst; the summary must not upgrade the level.

job_description:
Who we are
Founded in 2009, we are a global leader in logistics software, trusted by more than 4,000 companies in 60 countries. Our mission is to make every delivery on time, every time. We believe in ownership, curiosity and kindness, and we have been named a Great Place to Work four years in a row. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and we celebrate diversity in all its forms.

The role
Site Reliability Engineer (SRE), Platform team.
You will keep our multi-region platform on AWS reliable: define SLOs, run the on-call rotation, automate infrastructure with Terraform and reduce toil.

Requirements: 4+ years in SRE or DevOps roles, strong AWS and Terraform, Linux, incident management.

What we offer
Competitive salary, stock options, 30 days of holiday, a yearly wellness budget, a home-office allowance, free lunch on office days, a bike-to-work scheme, parental leave above the legal minimum, regular team off-sites and a modern office with a rooftop terrace. We look forward to hearing from you!

job_description:
Senior Product Manager, B2B SaaS (Billing)

Context
We build billing and subscription software for B2B SaaS companies. Our customers range from seed-stage startups to public companies, and our product sits at the heart of how they make money. Over the last two years we have tripled our revenue and we are now expanding into usage-based pricing, which is the biggest change to the product since it was founded.

The opportunity
As Senior Product Manager for the Billing area you will own the roadmap for invoicing, usage-based pricing and revenue recognition. You will work with a team of eight engineers, a product designer and a data analyst, and you will report to the VP of Product.

What you will do
- Talk to customers every week: finance teams, RevOps and engineering leaders.
- Turn what you learn into a clear strategy and a roadmap the team believes in.
- Write crisp problem statements and acceptance criteria, then work closely with engineering on delivery.
- Define success metrics for every launch and follow up on them after release.
- Partner with sales, marketing and customer success on launches and pricing changes.
- Make trade-offs between new features, reliability work and technical debt, and explain them.

What you bring
- 5+ years of product management, with at least 2 years on a B2B SaaS product.
- Experience with billing, payments or financial products is a strong plus.
- Comfort with data: you can write basic SQL or work closely with an analyst to answer your own questions.
- Excellent written communication; most of our decisions are made in documents.
- A track record of shipping products that customers pay for.

How we work
We are remote-first across Europe with quarterly in-person weeks. We favour small teams with clear ownership, written decisions and long-term thinking over short-term output.

Our hiring process
A 30-minute intro call, a product case discussion, a meeting with the team and a final conversation with the VP of Product. We aim to finish within three weeks and we give feedback at every step.
notes: Over 2,000 characters: the summary must still fit the cap and keep the product area.
